Part 3

PM_Combined <- PM_Combined |>
  mutate(year = lubridate::year(lubridate::mdy(Date)))


sites <- PM_Combined |>
  distinct(year, Site.Longitude, Site.Latitude)


california <- map_data("state") |>
  filter(region == "california")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data = california,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "white",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = sites,
    aes(
      x = Site.Longitude,
      y = Site.Latitude,
      color = factor(year)
    ),
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "California PM2.5 Monitoring Sites",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal ()

There are significantly more PM2.5 Monitoring Sites in 2022 compared to 2002

Part 4

table(PM_Combined$year)

 2002  2022 
15976 59918 
PM_summary <- PM_Combined |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarize(
    missing = mean(is.na(PM25)) * 100,
    negative = mean(PM25 < 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )

in 2002 there are 0 missing values and 0 values below PM 2.5, however, in 2022 there are 0 missing values and 35.9% of values that are below PM 2.5

Part 5

# Level 1 : State
state_summary <- PM_Combined |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarize(
    mean = mean(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
    minimum = min(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum = max(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
  )

ggplot(PM_Combined, aes(x = PM25, fill = factor(year))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, color = "pink") +
  facet_wrap(~ year) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of PM2.5 in California",
    x = "PM2.5",
    y = "Measurements",
    fill = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
## Between the 2 years there was a higher daily average of PM2.5 compared to 2022. However, the value of 302.5 reflecting in 2022 could show that the PM2.5 reached higher Maximum and Minimum Values
# Level 2 : County

#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 50

ggplot(
  PM_Combined,
  aes(
    x = PM25,
    y = County,
    fill = factor(year)
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE, outlier.shape = NA) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 75)) +
  labs(
    title = "PM2.5 Distribution by California County",
    x = "PM2.5",
    y = "County",
    fill = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
county_summary <- PM_Combined |>
  group_by(County, year) |>
  summarize(
    observations = sum(!is.na(PM25)),
    mean = round(mean(PM25, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    median = round(median(PM25, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    minimum = round(min(PM25, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    maximum = round(max(PM25, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    sd = round(sd(PM25, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
county_summary

# Level 3 : City 
LA <- PM_Combined |>
  filter(County == "Los Angeles")

#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 50
ggplot(LA, aes(
  x = PM25,
  fill = factor(year)
)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 20,
    alpha = 0.6,
    position = "identity"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Local.Site.Name, ncol = 3) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 50)) +
  labs(
    title = "PM2.5 by Location in Los Angeles County",
    x = "PM2.5",
    y = "Observations",
    fill = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

We can see that Overall the local sites in Los Angeles County had overall more observations of PM2.5 in 2022 reflecting that the concentration of air pollution did not decrease between 2002 and 2022.
